Roll up derived regions against named residue subsets

Source: R/residue_regions.R
residue_regions_subset_summary.Rd

A companion to residue_regions(): that function always scans every residue covered by any tested peptide - the unrestricted, data-driven "total" picture, deliberately not pre-restricted to any subset you might already suspect matters. This function takes that unrestricted result and a named list of residue subsets (e.g. structural domains) and reports, per subset, how much of it the data-driven regions actually cover - a cross-check for a structural hypothesis against the unconstrained result, not a replacement for it. Call residue_regions() once (it does the expensive per-peptide testing and clustering), then this function as many times as you like against different subset definitions - it's a cheap rollup over an already-computed result.

Usage

residue_regions_subset_summary(region_df, regions)

Arguments

region_df

the data.frame returned by residue_regions().

regions

named list of c(start, end) residue ranges to check against region_df, e.g. list(NTR = c(1, 85), ACD = c(86, 165)).

Value

data.frame with one row per named subset: subset, n_residues (subset size), n_residues_significant (residues in the subset covered by any region in region_df), frac_significant, n_regions_overlapping, and directions (comma-separated set of direction values among the overlapping regions, "" if none).

See also

residue_regions()

Examples

file_nm <- system.file("extdata", "All_results_table.csv", package = "HDXBoxeR")
a <- output_tp(file_nm, percent = FALSE)
#> Protein.States used: Unbound bound
#> Deut.times used: 3.00s 60.00s 1800.00s 72000.00s
#> 29 peptide row(s) dropped: 29 not measured in every state, 0 with fewer than 2 replicate value(s)
#> Number of replicates used: Unbound=3 bound=3
#> no csv file written
rr <- residue_regions(a, state1 = "Unbound", state2 = "bound", times = "1800.00s")
residue_regions_subset_summary(rr, regions = list(nterm = c(1, 100), cterm = c(101, 225)))
#>   subset n_residues n_residues_significant frac_significant
#> 1  nterm        100                      8            0.080
#> 2  cterm        125                     24            0.192
#>   n_regions_overlapping directions
#> 1                     2  protected
#> 2                     1  protected
